locator.text: Equation (7.19), p. 79, in the proof of Proposition 7.2

evidence: paper: \|V_m(v,w)\| \le C\,P(v)/P(w), \qquad 0 \le w \le v \le L_s, \quad m \neq 0.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean never defines a forward fundamental matrix V_m; it bounds the value of every solution of the homogeneous equation instead. homogeneous_forward_bound gives ‖u(v)‖ ≤ exp((D+4C)L)·(P(v)/P(a))·‖u(a)‖ on any [a,b] with b−a ≤ L·S, for every nonzero harmonic j, with a constant free of j; since V_m(v,w)x is by definition the value at v of the homogeneous solution equal to x at w, taking the supremum over ‖x‖ ≤ 1 gives ‖V_m(v,w)‖ ≤ C·P(v)/P(w) with C = exp((D+4C)L), which is (7.19). The operator A_m of (7.17) matches the Lean coefficient exactly: FrameData.coefficient j = modalOperator with damping j z = j²·viscosity z, i.e. diag(λ,−λ) − m²d·I₂ + E. The paper's uniformity in m (its 'the exponential in (7.18) is at most one') is FrameData.energy_bound / ViscousPropagator.high_harmonic_damping, which use j² ≥ 1 for j ≠ 0. The exponential factor is explicit in Lean rather than absorbed into C; slot_exponential_bound (and the hslot hypothesis of homogeneous_forward_bound) makes it a constant on a slot of length O(S_*).
